title: Localization and total-limit assembly from representative map equalities
statement: In the setting of [stage3-pur-scalar-tensor-limit-strict-witness], assume the corrected ordinary-source equation of [stage3-pur-scalar-tensor-limit-good-representatives] on every pair of good integral localization representatives, with the specified ordinary tensorator and completion maps. For the same integral constructible M,N and completed-tensor completeness proof as before, the canonical scalarTensorCompleted satisfies the completed total-limit square. The conclusion is unchanged.

proof.text: Use good-complex localization and product localization to obtain essential surjectivity on pairs.

Package scalarReduction and tensorReduction as natural transformations: whisker the realization transformations by reduction and compose with the coherent counits. Compose the two word maps after ordinary scalar extension using scalarTensorOrdinary and scalarCompletion. Their component equality is exactly the corrected representative hypothesis.

For two natural transformations with the same source and target, equality on the image of an essentially surjective functor implies equality everywhere: choose an isomorphism q(P) to X, use naturality on both sides and cancel its functor image. Apply this to the ordinary-source word maps at (M,N).

The source scalarCompletion is invertible on the complete E tensor. The independently proved scalarTensorCompleted_unitEquation identifies its composite with the canonical completed comparison with the prescribed ordinary tensorator and tensor of completion maps. Cancel this source completion from the transported equation to get the unchanged canonical completed conclusion.

old_proof.text: Use the established localization of flat-term K-flat good complexes and the product-localization theorem to obtain essential surjectivity of the functor on pairs. No new resolutions or change-of-rings preservation result is required here.

Package scalarReduction and tensorReduction as natural transformations: whisker the supplied realization transformations by reduction, then compose with the reduction/total-limit adjunction counits. Whisker their scalar/tensor composites by the coefficient total-limit functor. Their component equations are exactly the two composites in the hypothesis and conclusion.

For an essentially surjective q and natural transformations a:F to H and b:G to H, transport the equation beta followed by b equals a from q-images to an arbitrary X. Choose e:q(P) isomorphic to X and apply the image equation to F(e.hom) followed by beta followed by G(e.inv). Postcompose with H(e.hom); naturality of b and cancellation of e.inv followed by e.hom give F(e.hom) followed by beta followed by b(X). Naturality of a gives F(e.hom) followed by a(X). Cancel the isomorphism F(e.hom). This is the proved private transport_all_bridges lemma.

Apply this transport to the two natural composites and the given representative equality, taking X=(M.obj,N.obj) and beta to be the hom of the existing scalarTensorCompleted comparison. Unfold only the component formulas and the two equal-universe scalar-extension wrappers to identify the displayed conclusion.
